idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. (Its staging candidate v2.3.1-rc was also marked unhealthy.) Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed: an orchestrator error halted it after us-east, leaving the regions on mixed versions. A second attempt completed the rollback in us-west and eu-west. Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and look into the orchestrator error that halted the rollback.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all three regions, with about 18% of requests erroring. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Moving back to an already-released version didn't need change-manager approval.
- **First attempt only partly worked:** an orchestrator error stopped the rollback after us-east, so the regions were briefly on different versions. Trying the same rollback again finished us-west and eu-west.
- **Current state:** all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and about 0.2% of requests error.
- **Incident:** the first request to open it timed out. I retried with the same idempotency key, which stops a retry from creating a duplicate. There's only one incident, INC-0001. Its summary covers the failure, the rollback (including the halted first attempt) and two follow-ups:
  - find out why v2.3.1 fails (its pre-release build had also failed checks in staging)
  - look into the orchestrator error that stopped the first rollback

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
Only us-east was rolled back. I'll try the rollback again for the remaining regions. Rolling back to v2.3.0 is safe to repeat, since us-east is already on that version.
